tasks.title: repo skeleton, the one gate, and a bash test harness
acceptance: bin/ci.sh exists, is executable, and exits 0 on a tree with no tests
every tests/*.test.sh runs; any non-zero makes the whole gate non-zero and the failing suite is named
shellcheck is clean over bin/**.sh
the GitHub Actions workflow calls bin/ci.sh rather than restating its steps

tasks.title: fm-emit.sh, the only writer of the event log
acceptance: writes are serialised by a lock; 20 concurrent writers lose no lines and every line parses as JSON
an unknown type is rejected with a non-zero exit and nothing is written
an event carrying a summary must have both en and zh-TW, otherwise it is rejected
ci.sh fails if anything under bin/ or board/ appends to events.jsonl outside fm-emit.sh

tasks.title: fm-sync-prs.sh, which notices a merge on its own
acceptance: polls gh for pull request state and writes pr_opened, merged and closed back through fm-emit.sh
de-duplicates against the log by pull request number and state; running twice changes nothing
a merge the captain performs on GitHub is detected by the system itself, not reported to it by a person
exits non-zero without polluting the log when offline or when gh is not authenticated
tests drive it from recorded gh output and make no network call

tasks.title: fm-guard.sh and git hooks: nobody writes to main
acceptance: fm-guard.sh refuses main, master and a detached HEAD, and honours FM_PROTECTED
pre-commit blocks a commit on a protected branch and allows one on a feature branch
pre-push blocks a push whose target ref is a protected branch
the hooks are self-contained: they must not depend on bin/ existing in the worktree being committed to
branch protection on GitHub has enforce_admins on, since firstmate runs on the captain's own credentials

tasks.title: the adapter contract, the mock adapter, and the contract test
acceptance: mock.sh produces a scripted diff and reaches no network
the contract test pins the meaning of exit codes 0, 1 and 2
the contract test proves an adapter ran no git and no gh command
the contract test proves an adapter wrote nothing outside its worktree
claude.sh, cursor-agent.sh and gemini.sh all pass the same contract test

tasks.title: fm-gate.sh, the seven gates
acceptance: each of the seven gates has one passing and one blocking case, fourteen in all
gate 5 blocks a pull request whose new test stays green after the implementation is reverted
gate 5 passes a pull request whose new test goes red when the implementation is reverted
gate 4 blocks a diff that reaches outside the task's scope globs in tasks.json
gate 7 ignores an APPROVE string that did not come from the configured reviewer account
the exit code says which gate failed

tasks.title: fm-worker.sh: worktree, adapter, commit, pull request
acceptance: creates a worktree per task from main under state/worktrees/<task>
the prompt carries only the task spec, the relevant part of design.md, and skills/worker
commit and gh pr create are run by this script; the adapter never touches git
an adapter exiting 2 moves to the next vendor in config.yaml and emits vendor_unavailable
an adapter exiting 1 proceeds to the gates without falling back
the whole path runs on the mock adapter with no network

tasks.title: fm-review.sh: the reviewer sees only the diff
acceptance: the reviewer prompt contains the diff, the task spec and the acceptance criteria and nothing else
a test asserts the prompt contains no worker log, reasoning or worktree path
the reviewer's output is posted with gh pr comment by the script
only APPROVE:<task-id> is recognised by fm-gate.sh

tasks.title: fm-dispatch.sh: the DAG, the limit, and the green-light gate
acceptance: dispatches nothing and exits non-zero when the log holds no matching greenlit event
dispatches only tasks whose depends_on are all merged
never exceeds the concurrency in config.yaml
ci.sh fails when section 14 of design.md and tasks.json disagree

tasks.title: fm-decide.sh: a decision lands and firstmate wakes
acceptance: with bun present it uses fs.watch and returns within 200ms of the file appearing
without bun it falls back to a one-second poll with identical behaviour
it depends on neither fswatch, entr nor watchexec
a decision already on disk is not missed across a restart

tasks.title: board server: SSE, static files, hot reload
acceptance: binds 127.0.0.1 only
tails events.jsonl and pushes new events over SSE
a change under board/public/** pushes a reload event
no build step: bun run board/server.ts starts it
the SSE client reconnects on its own after a drop
the board reports only what the log already holds; it derives task stage from events rather than keeping its own view

tasks.title: board UI: the ship, the crew, the decision deck, the lanes, the log
acceptance: rewritten from the prototype in design/proposals, not copied from it
every crew pose is expressed as a .fig.s-<state> class so e2e asserts classes rather than diffing screenshots
status text belongs to its own figure and no two nameplates collide
drag a figure to turn it, drag the deck to turn the crew, double-click resets
prefers-reduced-motion is honoured
decks and hull are generated from one curve in one SVG, in the same projection as the crew; no mixing an elevation with perspective decks
every deck carries a bulwark and a riser wall, so a level reads as a level
brass is the only accent in the scene and the crew are the brightest layer
the ship has six rates from a one-mast cutter to a six-mast man-o'-war, up to 24 aboard; a crowd stacks onto more decks rather than stretching the hull
hull, decks, crew and bubbles all align to --deckY0 + row * --rowStep, and each deck plate is the same height so the crew plant to the same depth on every level
the whole sail hangs above the tallest crewman's head, asserted as sail.bottom <= highestHead.top
mast spacing follows the topmost deck's width and no mast sits outside it at any rate
the helm is a fixture of the topmost deck, placed by construction rather than by where firstmate happens to stand
the bow faces left, the end firstmate stands on, with the stern lantern to the right
barrel, port lid, muzzle flash and smoke all point the same way, toward the bow
gun ports and the figurehead render at fixed pixel sizes and do not deform with beam
the hull's gun ports, the flash positions and the sound schedule all come from one gun list; each flash sits exactly on its port and the number of reports equals the number of guns
twelve actions pooled by deck, with a separate pool for idle crew; with twelve or more aboard at least eight distinct actions are on screen at once
every action holds or stands at a prop; nothing mimes
each action declares its own arm animation and no state rule leaks one onto an action that did not
tools follow the job rather than the role, and state wins over action
crew alternate a weight shift and hop on independent offsets; shoes animate with their leg and the foot travels more than 6px per cycle
the hop animates translate rather than transform so it composes with the pose animations
each crewman carries a status bubble above his head with a tail pointing back at him, the border colour carrying state
deck spacing exceeds body height plus bubble height, so no bubble covers the crew on the deck above, verified from 3 to 24 aboard
the roster opens automatically once the bubbles drop the task title, and carries state, deck, task id and title, file scope, round, pull request and progress
the captain is drawn at the left of the decision deck, poses through idle, ready and order, and is draggable
the deck renders a merge card, the seven-gate checklist standing in for the diagram

a merge and an order each trigger an ahoy: the ship heels, guns or bell, the crew cheer, a banner. Sound is synthesised through Web Audio with no audio files, there is a mute control, and prefers-reduced-motion is honoured
nothing in the celebration covers what is being celebrated
shared numbers have one source: CSS custom properties are written from the JavaScript constants, never declared twice

tasks.title: i18n: dictionaries, the tw2cn table, the hardcoded-string lint
acceptance: ui.en.json and ui.zh-TW.json hold exactly the same keys, and no value is empty
every key the page asks for exists in the dictionary
tw2cn.tsv covers the terms that differ between the two vocabularies, every row is two columns, and no term is listed twice
zh-CN is derived from zh-TW by the table at display time, so there is no third dictionary to fall out of step
the page holds no hardcoded Chinese: every string a reader sees comes from the dictionary
switching language makes no network and no model call

tasks.title: the /open endpoint and the read-only diff viewer
acceptance: any non-localhost origin gets a 403
a path resolving outside the repository gets a 403, with a test for the .. route and the symlink route
the editor command comes from config.yaml and defaults to code
a read-only viewer can show a file and a branch diff without leaving the board
a branch name carrying a shell metacharacter is refused, and an unknown branch is a 404 rather than a 500
every path-taking endpoint shares one check: resolve fully, then insist the real path sits inside the real root

tasks.title: the decision API, including merge cards
acceptance: after a POST, state/decisions/<id>.json exists and is valid JSON
e2e: choosing on the board releases fm-decide.sh within one second
posting the same decision twice is idempotent and creates no second file
kind=merge is supported: the card shows the seven gates, the diff stat, the files and the pull request link, answered with merge, send back or hold
choosing merge runs gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch from the script; a test asserts no path exists for firstmate to merge without the board
the board never merges directly: it writes the decision and calls bin/fm-merge.sh, which validates the pull request number and its state first

tasks.title: Playwright e2e and the GitHub Actions workflow
acceptance: every e2e uses the mock adapter and calls no model
chrome snapshots run in all three languages; interaction flows run in zh-TW only
GitHub Actions runs bin/ci.sh, the same file the local gate runs
a full CI pass completes in under 60 seconds locally
the gate itself is asserted to run the browser suite, not only CI asserted not to
every zh-CN assertion pins an expected string, derived the way the board derives it
a board under test binds a free port rather than a guessed one
a fixture is removed whether the test passed or not
the language mechanisms are covered one at a time
the sixty-second budget is measured, not hoped for

tasks.title: fm-protocol.sh: round three and its violations
acceptance: rounds one and two are not policed
round three with no ASK-PASS-CRITERIA from the worker is a violation, exit 3
a reviewer who never posts CRITERIA-COMPLETE leaves the list open, exit 4
after the list closes, a comment must cite an item on it, carry REGRESSION:, or be the APPROVE; anything else is a violation, exit 5
a comment from anyone but the configured reviewer does not trip it
it counts and reports how many items the closed list held
every violation is emitted so the captain sees the reviewer drip-feeding
the suite runs from recorded comment payloads and makes no network call

tasks.title: fm-diagram.sh: decision diagrams and the board embed
acceptance: each decision produces D-*.en.html and D-*.zh-TW.html
zh-CN is produced by post-processing the text nodes through tw2cn.tsv
only decisions the captain must rule on produce a diagram; routine events do not
the board embeds them in an iframe and swaps src with the language
the suite that covers it lives where bin/ci.sh runs it
generated diagrams do not trip the hardcoded-string lint, which scans authored pages
requesting a decision draws its diagram, so the board never HEADs a file nobody wrote
a drawing authored for one language and not another is refused rather than served unevenly

tasks.title: fm-reconcile.sh: reconciling after a crash
acceptance: replaying events.jsonl rebuilds the whole state with no snapshot
walks state/worktrees and gh pr list to find orphans
a worker whose pid is gone is marked worker_crashed and redispatched
reconciling is idempotent: two runs leave the same state
a merged pull request whose event carried no task is repaired from the branch name
it prints what it would change and changes nothing with --dry-run

tasks.title: self-update and sync-skills
acceptance: a skill-update task travels the same pull request and the same seven gates as any other
no path exists that edits skills/ without a pull request, and a test asserts it
sync-skills imports into skills/vendor/ one way and never writes back
a lint fails on vendor-specific syntax inside skills/

tasks.title: fm-cleanup.sh: a worker removes its own worktree and nothing else
acceptance: removes state/worktrees/<task> and the branch's registration, after that task's pull request is merged
refuses any path that does not resolve to a direct child of the repository's own worktree root
refuses a path escaping through .. or through a symlink, with a test for each
refuses the repository root, the main worktree, and a path belonging to another repository
refuses while the pull request is still open, so an unmerged branch is never swept away
is idempotent: cleaning an already-clean task changes nothing and exits 0
every worktree lives under one root inside the repository, so the system stays self-contained

tasks.title: fm-run.sh: one turn of the whole loop, and an end-to-end proof of it
acceptance: fm-run.sh once dispatches what is ready and advances every task in flight by one step
it dispatches nothing before a greenlit event
all seven gates green asks the captain rather than merging
nothing merges until a decision file exists
an end-to-end suite runs dispatch to merged pull request with the mock adapter, a bare remote on disk and a gh stub - no network, no model
the suite asserts the log records greenlit, dispatched, commit_pushed, pr_opened, review_opened, decision_requested and merged
the worktree is gone after the merge

tasks.title: the adapter verdict: a vendor that fails silently is not one that worked
acceptance: an adapter reports unavailable when its CLI prints an outage and exits 0
a finished run whose own output discusses logins, rate limits or 429 is done, not an outage
a verdict reads only the bytes its own run added to the shared fallback log
each adapter is asserted to produce the invocation its CLI documents, not merely to be handed the prompt
the reviewer falls back through the same chain as the worker, from one implementation
no vendor runs twice however the fallback list is written
a review round must carry APPROVE or REJECT; anything else is an engine that failed, exits 3 and emits review_failed
a failed round keeps the engine's log under state/reviews and says where it is
fm-run reports a reviewer that was unavailable or produced no verdict instead of swallowing it
review_failed and worker_crashed read as blocked on the board, in counts as well as lanes
every stage the board maps is a type fm-emit will write
no stage of bin/ci.sh reads standard input, and a suite is handed /dev/null
the hygiene lint is asserted to be linting the suites it was given
no script dispatches a child without closing standard input, proved by a probe that blocks forever if it is open
the gate lints bin/adapters as well as bin, which bin/*.sh does not reach
work in the worktree is never discarded because the verdict read an outage
wording never decides finally: the caller supplies the evidence and work beats a signature
a vendor named in config.yaml with no adapter behind it is a configuration error, not an outage
a fixture that swaps a script out is paired with its restore by the harness, and a hand-rolled one fails the gate
the gate names every script that dispatches without closing standard input
an exit code never overrules produced work, in the adapters or in either caller
every signature is shaped like a failure and is read against a healthy transcript as well as a failing one
a configuration error is found before any vendor runs
each attempt reads only its own output: its own directory and its own slice of the shared log
a file that is meant to be sourced never carries the standard-input redirect

tasks.title: the option loop: eleven scripts spin for ever on a flag with no value
acceptance: no script loops for ever when a flag arrives with nothing after it
every one of them exits 64 and says which flag
the gate refuses a shift 2 that has not checked it has two
the probe runs under an alarm, because a test for a hang would hang the gate rather than fail it

tasks.title: the crew are agents, not pull requests
acceptance: a crewman is an agent that is working, not a task and not a pull request
the crew comes from the actors in the event log, derived by the server
an agent's bubble says which task it is on, and the roster says the same
two agents on two tasks are two crewmen; one agent that has moved between tasks is one
github is not an agent and is never aboard
the ship's rate follows the number of agents, which is the concurrency, not the backlog
the captain is not crew: he is drawn beside the cards, from the same pending deck the cards come from, and nothing else derives him
an agent that has finished its run is not aboard, whatever became of the task
a run says when it ends, on every exit path including the ones that give up
no script names a signal alongside EXIT in one trap: the handler runs and execution continues, and kill stops working
a suite that prints command-not-found cannot report green: the gate reads what the run said

tasks.title: one exit code for a usage error, in every script
acceptance: every usage error in every script exits 64, and every refusal to write exits 1
the gate enforces it rather than the design merely stating it
each converted path has an assertion that fails if it goes back

tasks.title: the pipe-into-grep lint is blind to the files that carry the lint
acceptance: the lint reads tests/ as well as bin/, which is where most of the pipelines are
a file is no longer exempted whole: a line says it quotes the shape rather than runs it, and every other line in that file is judged
every site the widened lint reports is converted to a here-string or marked, and the count is pinned so a new one cannot arrive unnoticed
the marker is tested from both sides: a marked line does not fire the stage and an unmarked one does
